transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-13 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Mark Johnson (CTO - Brightlane), Lea Gomez (ML Eng), Ravi Patel (Security)

Summary: Quick migration walkthrough focused on mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood API. Went through completions/chat parity, streaming, embeddings, token counting differences and recommendations for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private. Agreed to provide parity docs, security artifacts, and run a POC benchmark.

Topics covered: API parity, streaming mapping, function/tool calling differences, embeddings sizes, quantization/latency tradeoffs, KV cache, batching, Dedicated capacity, SOC2/KMS/VPC questions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. Good to meet you all.
[00:28] Mark: Hi Alex, thanks. We've been using a mix of OpenAI for chat, Anthropic for safety-filtered chat, and Together for high-throughput stuff - so lot of moving pieces.
[00:45] Priya: Cool, that's helpful. Today's demo we'll show parity mappings - how your current API calls map to Redwood, what changes you might need, and the ops choices (hosted, dedicated, or private). We'll also highlight token accounting and cost tradeoffs.
[01:15] Lea: Quick note - our embeddings pipeline is in production with OpenAI embeddings and a Pinecone vector store. We want the same dims and minimal drift.
[01:35] Alex: Totally. We'll show how Redwood embeddings align, and give an example script to swap model names and endpoint params.
[02:05] Mark: Biggest concerns: output parity (so downstream QA not broken), latency for real-time chat, and security/compliance.
[02:22] Priya: Understood. We'll cover function calling and streaming mapping - those are usual friction points - and then show dedicated options for low-latency.
[03:00] Alex: Starting with the API surface - Redwood uses a REST/SDK approach similar to others. For chat completions your OpenAI calls (messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop) map directly to Redwood's chat endpoint. Example:
[03:30] Alex: (reads) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
body: model: "redwood-2-chat", messages: [...] temperature: 0.2, max_tokens: 512, stop: ["\n\n"].
[04:05] Lea: How about Anthropic? We use their 'prompt' window and have some safety wrapper - is there a difference?
[04:22] Priya: Anthropic-style prompts map to Redwood's structured messages, but note that Anthropic sometimes has different tokenization heuristics which can cause slight token delta. We'll include a tokenizer mapping script.
[05:00] Alex: Also Together's streaming SDK we know customers use for low-latency token streaming; Redwood supports streaming responses with chunked SSE and SDK streaming hooks. Slightly different framing but same developer patterns.
[05:32] Mark: Token accounting - we bill per-token similar to others, but what about differences in tokenizer? Could cost estimates be off?
[05:48] Priya: Yes, tokenization differences can cause a 2-8% delta depending on prompts. We'll provide tokenization examples per model and a small script to normalize counts.
[06:20] Alex: Embeddings - Redwood supports multiple embedding models with dims 1024 and 1536; we can select the closest to your OpenAI model. For vector stores, same vectors, no change to Pinecone or we can suggest Redwood's optimized caching.
[06:55] Lea: Our pipeline expects 1536 dims from Ada. Is there a 1:1 mapping?
[07:10] Priya: There is a model that matches 1536 dims. We will show similarity scores and recommend minimal re-indexing steps.
[07:45] Mark: Performance - we saw p95 latency ~120ms on Together for short chat. We need <=150ms p95 in prod.
[08:03] Priya: With Dedicated GPUs and our optimized KV cache and batching policy you should be able to hit that. We demoed a similar workload last quarter - we'll share that benchmark.
[08:30] Alex: Important to call out: batching reduces cost but increases throughput latency tradeoff. For real-time chat we suggest small batch sizes + prefix KV cache enabled.
[09:05] Ravi: Security - we need SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration, and ability to run Private in a VPC. Also data residency for EU customers.
[09:22] Priya: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II (we'll share attestation), KMS/HSM integrations for key control, and a Private deployment option that can run in your VPC or on-prem. We'll include the architecture doc.
[09:58] Mark: How do we handle data retention and logs for compliance?
[10:12] Alex: You can configure audit log retention and opt out of logging for specific routes. For Private, logs stay in your environment. For Hosted, we support data retention policies and can sign addendums.
[10:45] Lea: Function/tool calling - Anthropic/Azure SDKs have slightly different sigs. How do we map?
[11:00] Priya: We support function calling; mapping is a simple param name swap in most SDK calls, and Redwood returns the same structured JSON. We've included a sample mapping: anthopic_func -> redwood.function_call with identical schema. (note: auto-transcription says 'anthopic' here).
[11:35] Alex: Now walking through a short demo - we'll show a sample chat call, streaming tokens, and an embeddings request.
[12:05] [screen share noise] Priya: Here's the Redwood Console - model catalog, latency dashboards, per-route cost breakdown. You can pin a model version and configure rollout policies (canary/A-B) from the UI.
[12:45] Mark: Can we see token breakdown per-session?
[12:58] Priya: Yes, token-level cost and per-route dashboards are available. We also show per-user or per-route percentile latency.
[13:30] Alex: Showing SDK snippet for swapping from OpenAI's completions to Redwood chat. (reads code) Change client import, model name, and the streaming handler - everything else is mostly identical.
[14:10] Lea: Great. For embeddings, do we need to re-embed to change dims?
[14:26] Priya: If your target model dims differ, re-embedding is needed. For our recommended 1536 match, re-embedding can be done incrementally; we suggest re-indexing in small batches and running QA similarity tests.
[15:00] Mark: Cost question - roughly how does Redwood hosted cost compare to OpenAI?
[15:18] Alex: It depends on model/latency. For high-throughput lower-precision quantized models we can be 20-40% cheaper on tokens and substantially cheaper on large-batch embedding workloads. We'll provide an estimate for your workload once you share token distribution.
[15:50] Ravi: For enterprise, is there an option to lock down traffic to stay within region? Residency?
[16:05] Priya: Yes, we have region routing and Private deployments. For Hosted we can route to EU regions and provide data residency contracts.
[16:40] Alex: Now a quick look at Dedicated - dedicated GPU pools you can reserve; low jitter network, predictable throughput and optional burst capacity for spikes.
[17:20] Mark: Ops wise, how much integration work to try a POC?
[17:32] Alex: Minimal - sample SDKs and parity scripts we send will let you run a few representative calls. For performance POC we can run side-by-side against your Together and OpenAI baselines.
[18:05] Lea: Anything special for quantized models? We run 4-bit quantization in the stack.
[18:20] Priya: Redwood supports quantization-friendly execution paths; we'll note the recommended model variants and kernel selections. There may be small output variance; we'll call that out in the parity doc.
[19:00] Alex: On monitoring, Redwood Console exposes tracing hooks to correlate request IDs back to your logs; that made debug easier for many customers.
[19:25] Mark: Good, we need request-id correlation for SRE.
[19:38] Priya: We'll also show the rollout UI - if a new model has regression you can automatic-fallback to previous model.
[20:05] Alex: Ok let's go through a concrete parity example - OpenAI chat completions call -> Redwood chat mapping, including function call example and streaming event sample.
[20:40] [demospeak] Alex: (typing) Here's the function payload; Redwood returns same 'name' and 'arguments' fields. You can wire the handler identically.
[21:10] Lea: Any gotchas with stop sequences? Some of our prompts depend on nuanced stopping.
[21:28] Priya: Stop sequences behave the same; only tokenization differences can cause off-by-one. We'll include examples to test and adjust stops.
[22:00] Mark: For embeddings drift tests, what's the recommended acceptance threshold?
[22:18] Priya: Typically 95%+ nearest-neighbor overlap for top-10 results; we'll provide our eval script so you can run it locally.
[22:50] Alex: Let's talk next steps - we'll send a parity mapping doc + SDK snippets, the security artifact pack (SOC2, KMS, VPC notes), and propose POC dates.
[23:15] Mark: Sounds good. On POC scope - we'd like to test chat latency, throughput, and embedding retrieval recall across a 2-week run.
[23:35] Alex: Perfect. We'll need a sample workload (token distribution, request per second targets, and embedding dataset size).
[24:02] Ravi: Also need to vet KMS key flow and audit log retention.
[24:20] Priya: We'll attach the KMS integration docs. On Private you'd manage the keys; for Hosted we can integrate customer KMS with key wrap.
[25:00] Lea: One more question - does Redwood support red-team style safety evals like Anthropic?
[25:18] Alex: We have quality monitoring and evaluation tooling in Redwood Optimize, and can configure regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll show the eval harness in the follow-up.
[25:45] Mark: Any mention of vendors for vector DBs - we use Pinecone but consider alternatives.
[26:00] Priya: We support all major vector stores; if you want we can show performance with both Pinecone and an S3-backed store.
[26:30] Alex: Quick pause - any blockers on your side to start the POC?
[26:45] Mark: Nothing legal yet; procurement will need the SOW and security pack. We do want a pricing estimate.
[27:05] Alex: We'll include a pilot pricing worksheet and optional Dedicated pricing.
[27:40] Lea: For SDK updates, do you have migration guides for Python/Node?
[27:55] Priya: Yes - we'll include Python and Node examples, plus a small script to re-tokenize and estimate cost delta.
[28:30] [minor crosstalk]
[29:00] Alex: Demo wrap-up - showed chat, streaming, embeddings, and console features.
[29:20] Priya: I'll follow up with the KMS and architecture docs.
[29:40] Mark: Thank you both - nothing else from Brightlane.
[30:00] Alex: Recap of action items and owners.
[30:18] Priya: We'll also propose POC metrics and a simple test harness you can run locally or have us run against your endpoints.
[31:00] Lea: Timeline-wise we can commit to providing workload by 2026-02-20.
[31:20] Alex: Great, plan to send docs by 2026-02-16 and 2026-02-18 per items.
[31:40] Mark: Let's tentatively schedule the POC start for 2026-02-24, two weeks.
[32:05] Alex: Works for us. Any final questions?
[32:20] Ravi: One last thing - we use SAML SSO and need RBAC integration; is that supported?
[32:35] Priya: Yes, SSO (SAML/OIDC) and RBAC are supported in the Console; for Private we can sync with your IdP.
[33:00] Alex: Ok we'll circulate the security pack and SSO docs.
[33:20] [wrap-up chatter]
[34:00] Mark: Thanks, this was useful.
[34:12] Alex: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the mapping doc and next steps.
[51:20] [call ends; mute noises]

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'anthopic', 'redwood dediate' in auto-generated sections). Shared artifacts referenced: parity-mapping.docx (will be sent), pilot-pricing.xlsx (will be sent), SOC2_attestation.pdf (will be sent), KMS_integration_notes.pdf (will be sent).
